museum_original_name: المتحف المصري بالقاهرة (Musée égyptien du Caire)
stated_count_source: No official crocodile total found. 1905 CG catalogue lists 11 young crocodile mummies (CG 29710-29720), 3 large mummies (CG 29628-29630), 1 head (CG 29578), 7 egg items (CG 29579-29585), 5 coffins/sheath (CG 29813-29816bis).
possible_additional_holdings: Basement: official page states boxes of 'Mummies of crocodiles' from the Japanese expedition at Tehna el-Gabal (Akoris) are stored in the basement (https://egyptianmuseumcairo.eg/the-basement-of-the-egyptian-museum/). Ikram & Iskander 2002 CG 'Non-human mummies' (print, not seen) likely re-catalogues crocodiles. Popular sources (Archaeology magazine 2004, Ikram) mention an ~18-ft crocodile with a baby crocodile in its mouth (candidate only). Ikram 2005 (Divine Creatures, pp. 16-43) cited by De Cupere et al. 2023 for evisceration in 'two sacred crocodiles from the Cairo Museum collection'.
scholarly_catalogue: Gaillard & Daressy 1905 (CG 29501-29733, 29751-29834); Ikram & Iskander 2002 (CG Non-human mummies, not seen)
image_license: UNKNOWN (site footer: 'Copyright © 2026 The Egyptian Museum'); 1905 catalogue plates public domain scan (archive.org, NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT)
api_url: UNKNOWN (WordPress REST API exists but artefact post type not exposed; no collection API)
notes: Official artefact page 'Mummies of the big Nile crocodile (Crocodilus niloticus)', Gallery 53 – Upper Floor, with photo of two large largely unwrapped bitumen-coated crocodile mummies. The 1905 CG entries are recorded individually as PROBABLE (catalogue >100 years old; some objects may have been transferred e.g. to NMEC/GEM/Kom Ombo Crocodile Museum - not verified). No online collection database.

stated_count_source: Official MoTA page gives no number of mummies; only 'The longest crocodile was 4.30 m, while the smallest was 2m' plus crocodile fetuses. MoTA brochure: Shutb cemetery 'Nearly 80 crocodiles were found'. News (candidate-only: youm7 2022-11-23, elbalad, coptstoday): '22 crocodiles of 50 found' and '5 mummies showing mummification'.
possible_additional_holdings: Crocodile fetuses/embryos, eggs (brochure: 'Crocodile mummies include crocodile eggs and embryos, small and large crocodiles' from al-Shutb); model eyes and gold/ivory teeth (replicas). Pottery coffins from el-Shatb cemetery (tomb model).
scholarly_catalogue: UNKNOWN (no catalogue found). El-Shatb excavations by Egyptian Antiquities Organization 1965-68, 1971-83 reported only in secondary web sources so far
image_license: UNKNOWN (MoTA brochure photos, no licence stated)
notes: Opened 2012 next to Kom Ombo temple. MoTA text (EN/AR): 'Its main exhibition hall displays the mummified mummies of Nile crocodiles' / 'تعرض قاعة العرض الرئيسية بالمتحف مومياوات مُحنطة لتماسيح النيل'. MoTA brochure p. 2 photos: a large linen-wrapped crocodile mummy with lattice bandaging plus smaller wrapped ones, and a row of large unwrapped mummies. A web-search summary attributed the sentence 'A selection of the surviving crocodile mummies from Kom Ombo are on display in the new Crocodile Museum near the temple that opened in 2012' to a scholarly source, but it is NOT in De Cupere et al. 2023 (full text checked) – origin unverified. No individual inventory numbers published online; no object rows created.

museum: Qubbat al-Hawa Project (Universidad de Jaén) – on-site store, tomb QH34ll
museum_original_name: Proyecto Qubbet el-Hawa, Universidad de Jaén / قبة الهوا (أسوان)
stated_count: 10 individuals (5 more or less complete bodies, 5 heads)
stated_count_source: De Cupere et al. 2023, PLOS ONE 18(1): e0279137, abstract and 'Description of the finds'
notes: Holding = on-site storage at Qubbat al-Hawa under MoTA / Spanish (Jaén) mission: 'The crocodile finds from tomb QH34ll have been studied on site and are also currently stored there.' Not a museum; status as of analysis in spring 2022.

possible_additional_holdings: Arabic news (candidate-only, via search snippets: youm7 2023-11-04, al-ain, elbalad) mention 'مومياء تمساح حديث الولادة' (mummy of a newborn crocodile).
notes: Egyptian State Information Service (official government portal, not the museum's own domain) states: 'The museum also displays a number of human mummies and a group of animal mummies, such as: crocodiles; cats; and fish.' and 'In the hall there are also a number of mummified animals ... such as: the ram; the cat; the ibis; the crocodile; and the monkey.' MoTA egymonuments page only says embalming was applied to animals '(Cats, dogs, crocodiles…. etc.)' – generic, not a holding statement. No object-level data online. sis.gov.eg required adding the missing Sectigo intermediate certificate (chain incomplete); beta.sis.gov.eg Arabic page blocked by WAF.

possible_additional_holdings: Arabic news (youm7 2025-05-18 via search snippet, candidate-only): reconstructed 'Crocodile Temple' inside the museum with 'مومياء لتمساح يتوسط المدخل' (a crocodile mummy in the middle of the entrance). Maspero.eg (state media, 2023-10-22) confirms only that the Crocodile Temple model was moved from the garden inside the museum (reopened Oct 2023).
inventory_numbers_known: Theadelphia wooden litter inv. 19679–19681 (per Shimizu 2026 n. 5 citing Kockelmann 2017, 614–615, Taf. 72, 77–78); crocodile mummy's own number UNKNOWN
scholarly_catalogue: Breccia 1922 guide (Room 9); Kockelmann 2017 (Ägyptologische Abhandlungen 74), 614–615, Taf. 72, 77–78 (not seen); Shimizu 2026, Orient 61, Fig. 5b
image_license: UNKNOWN (Shimizu 2026 Fig. 5b, © Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan)
notes: Shimizu 2026 (Orient 61: 109-125) Fig. 5b: 'Example of a crocodile mummy on a wooden litter (Graeco-Roman Museum, Alexandria; photograph by the author, 2024)' – confirms a crocodile mummy on display in 2024. Breccia 1922 (museum guide, Room 9): 'On the litter is the mummy of a crocodile. The wooden case and the litter were discovered in the temple of Theadelphia'. Provenance of the mummy itself not explicitly stated. Current MoTA page (EN/AR) says nothing about crocodiles.

museum: Akoris (Tehna el-Gebel) archaeological site – Chapel E storeroom, Western Temple (MoTA; Paleological Association of Japan mission)
museum_original_name: تهنا الجبل (أكوريس) / アコリス遺跡
stated_count_source: Shimizu 2026 n. 7 and p. 117: crocodile mummies kept in Chapel E (2024); 'Most crocodile mummies identified during the 2024 operations at Chapel E were smaller, under 4 m'
possible_additional_holdings: Crocodile coffins relocated by Abou-Seif 1926 into Chapel E; japanese web report (isan-no-sekai.jp 8208) photo of a crocodile mummy placed in the rock-cut temple; 'several crocodiles over 3.5 m' found in the temple
scholarly_catalogue: Shimizu forthcoming (Chapel E cleaning 2024); Abou-Seif 1926 ASAE 26: 32-38; Paleological Association of Japan 1995 (Akoris report)
notes: On-site storeroom, not a museum. Shimizu 2026: 'Currently (in 2024) the crocodile mummies in Akoris are kept inside Chapel E'; Abou-Seif (1926) relocated there crocodile mummies and coffins 'deemed unnecessary for the Cairo Museum'; iron gate installed, second room became storage. Part of the Akoris crocodile mummies went to the Egyptian Museum Cairo (see EMC basement page: 'Mummies of crocodiles ... from Japanese expedition at Tehna el-Gabal').
